title: Add class-of-work trend to athena status for OLY-9-10
summary: Give OLY-9-10 a mechanism: a new class-trend measure in athena-core that compares older and newer landed jobs per class of work (minutes), reports classes improving, and names the earlier landed job after which the class's cost rose. It is printed by `athena status` as a `trend` line and recorded in docs/spec.toml with measure ending `status: trend`. Audience: Hestia/the owner judging Phase 5.

defaults_applied.how: Unit tests for the module; fmt, clippy, test pass.
Criteria run tests that check improving/worse output.
Measure is enforced by status label test.
Absent output when history is too thin.
Doc comments written for outside readers.
BRIEF.md asks for tagged releases and a changelog, so the change records itself in CHANGELOG.md.

assumptions: Code survey: read crates/athena-core/src/status.rs (Throughput::compute, landed_jobs, StageMinutes, median, STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS, StatusView, test every_measure_label_names_a_status_view_field_and_a_printed_line), crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs (status text assembly near the throughput line), crates/athena-core/src/store.rs (JobRecords.job.class_of_work, Records::request_jobs) and crates/athena-core/src/hestia.rs (measure label check). No new record or data file is added under crates/, so check_record_file/AnyRecord/round-trip tests are not affected; the measure is computed directly from existing job records, not via a stand-in.

Design: new module crates/athena-core/src/class_trend.rs computes, per class_of_work (from the job record) with at least 4 landed jobs, the median total minutes of the older half against the newer half of landed_jobs(); a drop is 'improving', a rise is 'worse'. For a worsening class it names the landed job that begins the newer half's rise (the earliest job after which the class's minutes rose above the older median and stayed). StatusView gets a `class_trend` field, and STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS gets ("trend", "class_trend").
The spec.toml measure is rewritten to end with `status: trend`, and mechanism points at class_trend.rs, status.rs and display.rs.
Cost is measured as the existing minutes-per-landed-job (invocation, check and landing time), the comparable evidence available; token cost is out of scope.
No refusal rule is added or tightened, so no replay refusal-rate criterion applies.

acceptance_criteria.text: docs/spec.toml requirement OLY-9-10 has mechanism naming crates/athena-core/src/class_trend.rs (a file that exists), keeps owner Hestia, and a measure ending with `status: trend`; STATUS_MEASURE_LABELS in crates/athena-core/src/status.rs contains the `trend` label.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core class_trend`: a test builds landed jobs of one class whose minutes fall from older to newer and asserts the class is reported improving; another builds a class whose minutes rise after a named earlier job and asserts that job id is reported as making it worse; a class with too few jobs is not reported. These tests fail if compute returns nothing.

Run `cargo test -p athena-core every_measure_label_names_a_status_view_field_and_a_printed_line`: passes with the new `trend` label, proving StatusView has class_trend and `athena status` prints a line starting `trend `.
Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`: a status rendering test shows the `trend` line text with improving and worse classes; and the xtask/spec test over docs/spec.toml passes (`cargo test --workspace`).
`cargo fmt --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets` and `cargo test --workspace` all pass.
The trend section is absent (no line) when no class has enough landed jobs, so an empty history is not shown as success.

out_of_scope: Automatically reverting or proposing fixes for changes that made things worse
departures: Touches status wiring and a new analysis module, so cost is slightly above reference.
